name: Fish tacos with crunchy slaw
summary: Spiced, pan-fried hake flaked into warm wholewheat tortillas with a lime-yoghurt cabbage slaw, fresh tomato salsa and avocado, built at the table.
about: Fish tacos are street food from Baja California in north-west Mexico, where fish is tucked into tortillas with shredded cabbage, salsa and a creamy sauce. Hake, caught off the South African coast, is firm enough to pan-fry with spices and flake, and putting the fillings out in bowls lets everyone, children included, build their own.

ingredients.name: Limes
ingredients.note: zest of 1, juice of both; or 1 lemon

ingredients.name: Fresh coriander
ingredients.note: chopped, for the salsa and the slaw

ingredients.name: Hake fillets
ingredients.note: skinless, thawed if frozen and patted dry

steps: Make the slaw dressing: whisk the yoghurt with the zest of 1 lime, the juice of 1 lime and a pinch of salt in a large bowl.
Add the red and white cabbage, carrots and spring onions to the dressing and toss well. Set aside while you make the rest; the cabbage softens a little as it stands.
Make the salsa: mix the tomatoes, red onion and half the coriander with the juice of the second lime and a pinch of salt in a small bowl. Stir the rest of the coriander into the slaw.
Mix the cumin, paprika, garlic powder and salt and sprinkle it over both sides of the hake.

Heat the oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Lay in the fillets and cook, without moving them, for 3 minutes, until golden underneath. Turn carefully and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more, until the flesh is white all the way through and flakes when pressed with a fork.
Lift the fish onto a plate and break it into large flakes, checking for bones as you go.
Wipe the pan, put it back over medium heat and warm the tortillas one at a time for about 20 seconds a side, until soft and flecked brown. Stack them in a clean tea towel to keep warm.
Serve everything at the table: fill each tortilla with slaw, fish, salsa and a few slices of avocado, and fold.
prepNote: Shred the cabbage and carrot in the morning and keep them chilled; dress the slaw and cook the fish just before eating.
